findings.claim: The single mandatory seam task couples independently implementable native transport and canonical schema work to the external actor-routing integration, so unavailable peer actor source can stall work that does not consume it.
findings.location: artifact.md: Follow-on and implementation ownership; tree-settled.json tasks ht-qhz.1, ht-qhz.3 and ht-qhz.2.1
findings.evidence: The root requires that “only actual blocking shared boundaries gate their integration leaf, no global HOLD.” Yet ht-qhz.1 must land compilable protocol/CLI/journal dispatch wiring, consumes the “peer actor-route/classify_original_actor seam,” and requires original actor classification before new journal retry. Both ht-qhz.3 (typed native socket creation) and ht-qhz.2.1 (schema and canonical identity persistence) depend on completion of that entire task even though their consumed boundary is the topology data contract, not actor-route integration. The artifact provides no independently completable contract-only prerequisite or deferred actor-wiring subtask. Splitting the pure topology type boundary from actor-dependent dispatch would retain the declared interfaces without making that external integration a gate for these unrelated deliverables.
